description: Two-panel SEM fracture-surface group (secondary-electron imaging) of Charpy V-notch (CVN) specimens of an Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel; both panels carry a printed 20 µm scale bar in the lower right corner, neither carries axis labels or a panel marker, and they are read by morphology. (a) As-hot-rolled specimen: the field is dominated by large flat, angular cleavage facets bounded by sharp tear ridges; the facet faces show fine parallel slip traces and river-like steps, with only minor ductile ridging — a brittle, transgranular cleavage appearance. (b) Hot-rolled, solution-treated for 10 min at 1100 °C and water-quenched specimen: the surface is heavily rumpled and made of rounded, roughly equiaxed units separated by a network of fine dimples and tear ridges, with no large flat facets — a ductile, dimple-rupture appearance at comparable magnification. Together the two micrographs demonstrate that the same steel changes from brittle cleavage fracture to fully ductile fracture after solution treatment and quenching. The only number printed on the images is the 20 µm scale bar.

subfigures.description: SEM image of the CVN fracture surface of the as-hot-rolled Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel, 20 µm scale bar. Large flat angular facets with sharp tear ridges and fine parallel slip traces / river lines on the facet faces; small ductile ridges only occasionally.

SEM image of the CVN fracture surface of the hot-rolled, solution-treated (10 min at 1100 °C) and quenched Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel, 20 µm scale bar. Rounded equiaxed units separated by networks of fine dimples and tear ridges; no large flat cleavage facets visible.

observations.observation: Both panels are SEM fracture-surface images with a printed 20 µm scale bar in the lower right corner; no axis labels are present.
Panel (a) shows large flat, angular facets bounded by sharp tear ridges, with fine parallel slip traces/river lines on the facet surfaces.
Panel (b) shows rounded, roughly equiaxed units separated by a network of fine dimples and tear ridges, with no large flat facets.

The caption states that (a) is the CVN fracture surface of the as-hot-rolled specimen, where fracture was mainly transgranular cleavage with {111} slip traces on the cleavage facets, indicating brittle fracture due to j-carbide precipitation.
The caption states that (b) is the specimen solution treated for 10 min at 1100 °C and that its fracture mode is completely ductile.
The specimens are Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel (nominal composition as printed in the caption).
The caption writes the precipitate as 'j-carbide'; this corresponds to the κ-carbide referred to elsewhere in the citing text.
The citing text states the as-hot-rolled CVN breaking energy was only 23 J in the L–T orientation and 22 J in the T–L orientation.

The citing text states that solution treating for 10 min at 1100 °C and water quenching improved toughness to an average of 160 J (L–T orientation), with completely ductile fracture as shown in Fig. 13b.
The citing text states that the cleavage facets displayed slip traces at roughly 60° from one another, indicating fracture by decohesion of active slip planes.

The citing text attributes the large energy difference between hot-rolled and hot-rolled plus solution-treated conditions to SRO and precipitation of j-carbide, because the hot-rolled material was slow cooled after deformation.
The citing text gives the compared reference material as a hot-rolled Fe-30Mn-9Al-2.7Si-0.9C steel with 0.023% P and an average grain size of 50 µm.

unreadable_items: No panel letters (a)/(b) are printed inside the images; panel identity relies on the caption and reading order.
No magnification or accelerating voltage is given on either image.
